entities.description: The canonical entity-relationship graph between data objects, independent of any specific solution's implementation. Captures directed relationships like User owns Asset (1:N, composition), Customer places Order (1:N, reference), Employee works on Project (M:N, association), Customer is a Person (1:1, inheritance). Carries both cardinality (Cardinality) and structural kind (Kind) so the catalog distinguishes ownership from loose reference from peer association from subtype. Self-references are allowed (User directly manages User).

computed_fields.name: data_object_relationship_label
computed_fields.description: Composed from the source data object name, the relationship verb, and the target data object name. Recomputed on every write so renames in either parent flow through.

computed_fields.name: owner_side
computed_fields.description: The parent side is the one side of the cardinality, so it is derived and cannot disagree with it. Kept as written for one_to_one and many_to_many, where cardinality does not decide it.

validation_rules.name: users_link_is_not_many_to_many_reference
validation_rules.message: A reference to users is one person per record. Use one one_to_many link from users per role, or a junction entity or an association for a genuine panel or team.
validation_rules.description: Check B7b. A row-scope rule needs a single owner, and a role on a record is one person.

entities.description: Authored operational persona for a domain; an RBAC input (reach via role_modules, gates via process_raci). Replaces the deleted _core model roles.
Authored RACI assignment linking a process to a polymorphic actor (a domain_role persona XOR an agent skill), with the raci letter and consultation_blocking. Exactly one actor per row.

validation_rules.name: exactly_one_actor
validation_rules.message: A process_raci row must reference exactly one actor: a domain role or a skill, not both and not neither.
validation_rules.description: Polymorphic RACI actor: persona (actor_role_id) XOR agent skill (actor_skill_id).

entities.description: Junction: which modules does this role touch, and how heavily. `interaction_level` is two-value (`primary` / `secondary`) — read-only-ness is captured by the role's permission bundle holding only `:read` for that module, not a separate axis. Per plan-roles.md §7 Q1 resolution. The 2-module floor (§7 Q5) is enforced by the loader, not at the DB level.

fields.title: From Data Object
fields.description: The source / subject side of the relationship

fields.title: To Data Object
fields.description: The target / object side of the relationship

fields.title: Cardinality
fields.description: Standard ER cardinality between the two data objects

fields.title: Kind
fields.description: Structural role of the relationship, orthogonal to cardinality: `composition` (parent owns child, cascade), `reference` (loose link, no cascade), `association` (peer-to-peer M:N), `inheritance` (subtype / IS-A)

fields.title: Verb
fields.description: Parent-voice verb describing the relationship (owns, manages, places, is assigned to)

fields.title: Inverse Verb
fields.description: Reverse-direction phrasing for navigation (is owned by, reports to)

fields.title: Owner Side
fields.description: The parent side of the link: the lifecycle owner, and the end without the foreign key. Derived from relationship_type for one_to_many (source) and many_to_one (target). Set by hand only for one_to_one.

fields.title: Role Code
fields.description: Stable natural-key code for the persona (e.g. RECRUITING-RECRUITER).

fields.title: Description
fields.description: What this persona does and why it exists.

fields.title: Business Function
fields.description: Optional function scoping for the persona.

fields.title: Consultation Blocking
fields.description: For C (consulted) rows: input required/blocking vs advisory.

fields.title: Actor Skill
fields.description: Agent-skill actor (XOR actor_role_id); populated when process-skills land.

fields.title: Role
fields.description: The role that touches this module.

fields.title: Module
fields.description: The catalog module this role interacts with.

fields.title: Interaction Level
fields.description: How heavily this role touches this module. `primary` = the role can't function without this module (drives the role-union on-ramp per plan-roles.md §5.1). `secondary` = the role uses this module supportively or read-only.

fields.title: Notes
fields.description: Optional. Why this role touches this module at this interaction level.

fields.title: Required
fields.description: True when a link's field must be filled in once both entities exist. It never makes an entity required: whether an entity installs is is_install_optional on domain_module_data_objects (SKILL.md Rule #16). A required link to an absent entity carries no constraint.

domain_roles.description: Front-line sales leader who inspects pipeline by deal risk, runs forecast roll-ups, and coaches reps on recorded calls.
RevOps analyst who tunes deal-scoring and forecasting models, monitors forecast accuracy, and curates activity-attribution rules.
Quota-carrying rep whose activities are auto-captured, who submits a periodic forecast, and who acts on deal warnings and coaching.
Enablement coach who reviews recorded calls against the playbook and runs structured coaching sessions.
Owns the requisition-to-offer pipeline for assigned reqs: sources, screens, schedules, drafts and sends offers, drives candidates to hire.
Builds and works talent pools and the candidate CRM; generates qualified pipeline ahead of open reqs.
Owns interview logistics and offer / pre-employee paperwork; schedules panels and keeps the process moving.
Accountable for the recruiting function's output: approves reqs and offers, owns pipeline health and vendor relationships.
The role owning the open position. Cross-functional (sits in the hiring department, not Recruiting): defines the req, interviews, decides the hire, approves the offer.
Owns hiring-compliance surfaces: background-check adjudication, FCRA / adverse-action, EEO / OFCCP, and candidate data-subject requests.
PMO / BizOps lead who owns cross-team programs, triages intake, and rolls up OKR progress from work items.
Individual contributor who executes assigned work items, posts updates, and submits cross-team requests through intake.
Marketing operator who runs campaign projects with creative review and routes creative requests through intake queues.
Cross-functional objective owner who commits and scores OKRs and links key results to executing work items.

IT Operations persona that runs day-to-day SaaS administration: discovering and triaging applications, managing integrations and owners, optimizing license usage and reclamation, and operating automation workflows and self-service requests.

Procurement persona that owns the commercial SaaS lifecycle: renewal pipeline, vendor negotiations, spend allocation, and vendor risk attestation, with read access to discovery and usage data that informs renewal decisions.

IT Asset Management persona that governs the SaaS portfolio end to end across discovery, optimization, renewal, and automation; the cross-module owner accountable for portfolio cost, compliance, and lifecycle.
Owns the end-to-end contingent-workforce program: requisition intake, supplier distribution, rate-card governance, and the time-to-invoice flow. Spans worker sourcing and time-and-invoicing.
Governs the staffing-supplier panel and the rate cards: onboards and activates suppliers, approves rate cards by role and region, and monitors supplier performance against billed invoices.
Coordinates day-to-day contingent-labor operations: shepherds worker assignments and tenure tracking in sourcing, and chases timesheet approvals and invoice matching in time-and-invoicing.

Owns day-to-day operation of the learning platform: maintains the course catalog, manages enrollments and learning paths, configures automation and audiences, and administers credentials and continuing education.
Authors and versions courses, lessons, content assets, and assessments; publishes new training and retires outdated material across self-paced and instructor-led delivery.
Delivers instructor-led and virtual instructor-led sessions: runs scheduled offerings, records attendance, grades assessments, and supports learners through completion and certification.

Runs regulatory and policy training programs end to end: schedules compliance campaigns, tracks assignment completion, assembles training evidence, manages recertification, and produces regulator filings.
Cross-functional people leader who assigns and nudges direct reports through required and developmental learning, monitors completion and certification status, and follows up on overdue training.

Owns client engagements end to end: scopes the project, structures tasks and milestones, requests staffing, and drives delivery to completion. Accountable for on-time, on-scope delivery and for the project's billing readiness.

Owns the staffing and capacity workflow: matches skilled people to project demand, plans and commits resource allocations, confirms and releases assignments, and watches utilization and skill gaps across the billable workforce.

The billable practitioner who executes assigned project tasks and logs time and expenses against the engagements they work. Drives tasks to completion and submits clean actuals for approval and billing.

Owns project billing and revenue: manages budgets and rate cards, invoices reached milestones and approved time, and recognizes project revenue. Accountable for accurate, auditable project financials feeding the general ledger.

Accountable for the contract lifecycle end to end: owns the repository, signs off on approvals and executions, drives obligation tracking and renewals, and keeps authoring and negotiation moving across the team.
Runs the day-to-day contract workflow: assembles drafts from approved templates, shepherds signature envelopes, tracks obligations to closure, and processes renewals ahead of expiry.
Reviews and approves contract language, clause and template content, and redlines counterparty terms during negotiation. The legal gate on what the organization is willing to sign.
Bridges sourcing and contracting: turns awarded sourcing outcomes into draft agreements, consults on supplier terms during negotiation, and reads the repository for active supplier commitments.

Administers the HCM system of record: configures and maintains worker data, the org-unit structure, the job and position catalog, and the lifecycle workflow configuration. Holds admin authority across all HCM modules.

Executes the day-to-day worker lifecycle: processes hires into active workers, transfers and other employment events, leaves of absence, contract changes, and terminations. The transactional HR operator.
Advises managers on org changes, workforce moves, and employee relations. Accountable for sensitive lifecycle changes in their business unit and consulted on position and reorganization decisions.
Models the organization: authors and publishes job profiles, defines and approves positions against budgeted headcount, and maintains the org-unit hierarchy through reorganizations.

Owns an assigned product area end to end: triages feedback and feature requests in discovery, prioritizes and accepts work onto the roadmap, and shepherds features, releases, and beta programs from planning through ship.

Accountable for the product function's output: approves the published roadmap, owns product-line strategy and lifecycle transitions, and signs off prioritization and launch decisions across the portfolio.
Runs product operations: keeps roadmap and backlog hygiene, instruments and reports adoption and quality metrics, and coordinates release and beta logistics across teams.
Leads delivery of prioritized product work: takes accepted features through in-delivery and release, reports shipped and rolled-back states, and feeds feasibility input back into discovery.
Owns the marketing automation platform: configures campaigns, journeys, lead scoring, and forms, and keeps the program running across modules.
Plans and runs marketing campaigns and nurture journeys end to end, from authoring through launch and follow-up.
Frontline HR service agent: picks up employee cases from the portal queue, triages and classifies them, works them to resolution, and attaches knowledge. Reopens closed cases when something changes.

Accountable for HR service delivery output: owns the case queue, SLAs, routing rules, and the approval gate. Oversees workload, aging, and escalations across the case workflow and the employee portal.
Owns the HR knowledge base: curates and publishes articles, organizes them by case category, and promotes resolved cases into reusable knowledge to deflect future requests.
Owns the intranet governance program across all connected sources: sets policy, oversees recertification, and is accountable for content currency and accountability coverage.
Accountable owner for specific pieces of intranet content; responds to recertification attestations and remediates or archives stale content.
Connects and maintains intranet sources, runs crawls and scans, and keeps the inventory and connectors healthy.
Day-to-day governance operator: authors and publishes glossary terms, proposes and approves data classifications, manages stewardship assignments, and certifies assets within a data domain.
Accountable owner of a set of data assets and data products: grants and revokes certifications, signs off access policies, and is accountable for the asset's fitness for production use.
Operates the catalog platform itself: configures and runs metadata crawlers, manages lineage capture, maintains data domains, and curates the data-product marketplace surface.
Cross-functional governance authority spanning Data Engineering and GRC: sets classification and access policy, signs off enterprise data policies, and owns regulatory mapping of the data estate.
Analyst or data-product consumer who discovers assets in the catalog, reads glossary and lineage to build trust, and requests access to governed data products through policy.
Builds and publishes the product catalog, runs the storefront, and launches coupons and promotions. Reads order activity to see what is selling and adjust merchandising.
Runs the order-to-cash flow end to end: captures carts, completes checkouts and payments, creates orders, and drives them through fulfillment and shipping. Cross-functional operations persona.
Picks, packs, and ships paid orders and manages shipments and returns. Reads order detail to fulfill against the right line items.
Owns the enterprise process architecture: maintains capability maps, governs the process model repository, and aligns value streams to strategy.
Models and analyzes business processes and value streams, runs simulations, and prepares models for review and publication.
Accountable for one or more published business processes: approves publication, sponsors reengineering, and owns process outcomes. Cross-functional persona.

Owns the corporate travel program: sets and maintains travel policy, configures the approval workflow, monitors program spend and supplier performance, and is accountable for duty-of-care readiness across the organization.
Books and manages travel on behalf of one or more travelers: shops policy-aware fares, holds and tickets reservations, builds and amends itineraries, and reapplies unused-ticket credits.

Cross-functional self-service traveler: self-books within policy, maintains their own traveler profile, submits pre-trip approval requests, views and changes their own itinerary, and acknowledges duty-of-care alerts affecting them.
Owns the end-to-end marketing planning and budget process: builds and approves plans, sets budgets, oversees allocation and spend-to-plan reconciliation, and reports plan-level performance.
Authors marketing plans and plan lines, maintains the marketing calendar, and works with budget owners to align plan lines to allocated budget.

Cross-functional owner of marketing budget governance: approves budgets and allocations, monitors spend against plan, and reconciles committed and actual spend. Often sits in or partners with Finance.

Owns the site safety program: incident investigation, hazard and risk assessment, corrective actions, inspections, and required training. Accountable for closing incidents and verifying corrective actions.
Plans and runs exposure monitoring and industrial-hygiene sampling, manages occupational-health surveillance, and governs the chemical inventory and safety data sheets.
Owns environmental permits, conditions, and limits, emissions and release records, and ISO 14001 conformance; accountable for permit renewals and environmental reporting.
Cross-functional site leader accountable for the whole EHS program at an establishment, spanning safety, occupational health, environmental compliance, and audit readiness.
Prepares lease accounting: classifies leases, maintains right-of-use and liability schedules, records modifications and remeasurements, and generates the journal entries for the general ledger.
Maintains the lease record system: agreements and documents, critical dates and alerts, renewals and terminations, and the payment terms that feed lease accounting.
Owns lease-accounting policy and the close: approves classifications and modifications, reviews and files disclosures, and signs off on the lease subledger for financial reporting.
Runs the whole grazing operation: oversees herd performance, grazing plans, sales, and compliance across all properties and mobs.
Manages the animals and mobs day to day: records, weights, breeding, treatments, and movements in the yard and paddock.
Plans and executes pasture rotations: allocates paddocks, sets rest periods, and matches stocking rate to carrying capacity, moving mobs accordingly.
Owns the paid social estate: campaign strategy, budget allocation across platforms, and overall performance against targets. Accountable for spend and results.
Operates day-to-day optimization: bid and budget tuning, audience iteration, pacing, and responding to threshold breaches across ad sets.
Owns ad creative: concepts and variants, dynamic creative optimization rules, and the creative approval workflow that feeds live campaigns.
Triages insider-risk alerts, tunes detection indicators, and drives day-to-day monitoring of user risk across the workforce.
Investigates escalated insider-risk cases end to end: builds the activity timeline, performs file-lineage forensics, collects evidence, and packages it for HR and Legal.
Owns the insider risk program: approves case dispositions, governs HR/Legal escalation, and oversees exit-risk monitoring policy.

Designs and deploys executable process definitions and decision tables, owns versioning and breaking-change governance, and decides the orchestration topology across the engine and the case and decision layer.
Runs the live engine: monitors running instances, triages and resolves incidents, suspends or terminates stuck instances, and keeps throughput healthy across the execution and case modules.
Works the human side of orchestrated processes: claims and completes human tasks, advances case files with ad-hoc activities and milestones, and escalates when work stalls.
Configures channels, audiences, checklist templates, and learning modules, and authors and schedules company-wide frontline broadcasts and recognition programs.

Store, plant, or field manager who cascades broadcasts to their team, assigns and verifies tasks, approves shift swaps, and recognizes workers. Cross-functional: reports into store or plant operations, not internal comms.

Deskless worker who reads and acknowledges broadcasts, completes and submits tasks and checklists, requests and claims shift swaps, finishes microlearning, and sends and receives recognition from a mobile or shared device.

Owns the employee advocacy program end to end: enrolls advocates, sets topics and goals, runs campaigns, oversees gamification and rewards, and reports reach and pipeline impact to marketing leadership.
Sources, writes, and approves shareable content and suggested share copy, organizes it into topic streams, and keeps the advocate feed and newsletters fresh and on-brand.
An enrolled employee who reshares curated content to their personal social networks, earns points and recognition, and represents the employer brand to their own audience.
Runs the short-term rental operation end to end: listings, bookings, guest experience, turnovers, and owner reporting.
Owns listing distribution and nightly pricing: channel connections, rate plans, and dynamic-pricing rules.
Handles guest communication and bookings and coordinates turnovers so each guest has a smooth stay.
Schedules and verifies housekeeping and turnover work against the booking calendar.
Produces owner statements and payouts and handles lodging-tax filing and permit compliance.
Runs the marina end to end: oversees slip inventory and assignment, reservations, the boatyard, billing, and the fuel dock.
Assigns slips, handles transient arrivals and departures, and keeps the dock and assignment board current.
Handles reservations, boater and vessel records, document collection, and front-desk billing inquiries.
Runs the boatyard: estimates and work orders, haul-out and launch scheduling, and pump-out logging.
Owns contracts, recurring and metered billing, invoicing, and fuel and store reconciliation.
Owns the operator's booking operation: configures products, departures, and rates, oversees bookings, refunds, guide scheduling, and waiver compliance, and manages distribution.
Front-line staff who take and amend bookings over the phone, at the counter, and online, collect payments, and ensure each guest has signed a waiver.
Field staff assigned to departures: confirm availability, review the manifest and participant requirements, check out equipment, and run the trip.
Manages reseller and online-travel-agency relationships, maps products to channels, sets commission terms, and keeps channel availability in sync with the operator calendar.
Owns the shipper's freight operation: accountable for tendering, carrier performance, freight spend, and claims.
Turns orders into shipments, selects carriers, tenders loads, and works exceptions until delivery.
Runs carrier bids, negotiates agreements, and keeps contracted rates current.
Audits carrier invoices against shipments and contracted rates, works disputes, and files claims.
Manages the dock calendar at a shipper's facility and confirms appointments.
Runs a trucking company's freight operation: accountable for what gets booked and dispatched, what customers are billed, and what drivers and partners are paid.
Books and answers tendered loads, plans trips, assigns trucks and drivers, and works problems on the road.
Finds and vets partner carriers, posts loads to boards, and covers loads the company's own trucks cannot.
Rates delivered loads, assembles paperwork, issues invoices to customers, and handles cargo claims.
Calculates driver and owner-operator pay, applies deductions and escrow, and keeps owner-operator leases in order.
Runs an LTL terminal: freight bills, dock doors, pickup and delivery routes, and linehaul departures.
